continuity.narrative_arc: The cowherds ask about Krishna's birth and hear Garga's prophecy; humbled Indra and Surabhi honor Krishna as Govinda; Gokula prospers; Krishna retrieves Nanda from Varuna and reveals Vaikuntha to the cowherds before the closing praise.
continuity.krishna_form_contract: Use the established krishna-vrindavan-youth contract wherever youthful cowherd Krishna appears: deep matte blue skin, long dark curly hair, yellow dhoti, muted red-orange shawl, a plain smooth forehead, and one simple low gold band with one upright peacock feather. He has one face, two attached arms and hands, and two legs and feet. Never use an infant face, tall crown, forehead mark, or duplicate Krishna. In stanza 8 Vaikuntha is a revealed realm around him, not a second Krishna body; any separate Vishnu icon has its own one head and four arms.
continuity.supporting_people_contract: Nandagopan is a mature, moustached cowherd in simple cream and muted olive/green clothing. Gopas are a small group of individually distinct, naturally proportioned people. All ordinary people have two arms and two legs with connected hands and feet. Keep faces, limbs and clothing distinct; no clones, fused bodies or detached parts.

deity_contracts.indra: Indra is an adult male deity with one head and two arms, a modest painted-ochre crown, simple muted celestial garments and no peacock feather. Bowing and ritual actions must have connected natural hands. No thunderbolt unless explicitly required by a stanza; it is not required here.
deity_contracts.surabhi: Surabhi is one coherent sacred cow with natural bovine anatomy and four legs; she is distinct from Airavata.
deity_contracts.airavata: Airavata is one coherent pale elephant with natural elephant anatomy, four legs and a connected trunk; no extra heads or limbs. The source caption and approved Airavata character contract require exactly four distinct tusks rooted in the mouth region in two pairs.
deity_contracts.varuna: Varuna is a calm adult water deity with one head and two arms, a simple painted crown and muted water-toned garments; do not add unsupported weapons or additional arms. His attendants are not needed.

continuity.palette_contract: Flat, opaque matte South Indian temple-mural painting with broad mineral fields and firm dark drawn contours; warm cream, earth ochre, deep maroon, muted olive and deep blue Krishna. Ordinary human skin must read as warm brown: skin-only 15x15-pixel patch medians should have red-minus-blue under 120. Youthful Krishna must remain deep indigo-blue with blue-minus-red at least 40.
